items.title: Sales of Thélyson Orélien's novel skyrocket despite AI and plagiarism accusations
items.excerpt: Two weeks after the X account 'Balance ton Claude' accused Thélyson Orélien of writing most of his award-winning novel C'était ça ou mourir with generative AI, sales of the book have surged rather than collapsed.

items.title: BMJ Group, Sage and more to share 20m research papers with AI company Redpine
items.excerpt: Five academic publishers (BMJ Group, Sage, IOP Publishing, IGI Global and Wanfang Data) struck a deal giving Redpine's AI agents licensed access to 20 million peer-reviewed papers, a new licensing model for publisher content.

items.title: OpenAI 'trained models' on books from 'sketchy AF' LibGen, unsealed court filings reveal
items.excerpt: Unsealed filings in the authors' case show OpenAI staff discussed training early GPT models on Library Genesis books, debated how to describe the source publicly, and weighed the cost of buying books instead.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Historian Jill Lepore Speaks of an Industry—and a World—'On the Knife Edge of History'
items.excerpt: At Frankfurt's opening press conference, where AI was called 'the issue on everyone's minds', Jill Lepore warned against handing the future to tech moguls, and German publishers' chair Sebastian Guggolz said AI cannot make up for falling reading competence.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Program Picks
items.excerpt: Selected Frankfurt 2026 sessions include 'AI Narration Beyond the Lab: Use Cases, Business Models and Listener Acceptance' and a look at how rights trading changes in an AI-driven environment.

items.title: Kevin Roose Didn't Use AI to Write His Book About AI
items.excerpt: On WIRED's Big Interview, the author of The AGI Chronicles says his book 'was written by a very tired, overworked, under-slept human being', and talks about where AI fits, and doesn't, in writing a book.

items.title: LibreOffice says 'no AI' is now a software feature
items.excerpt: The open-source document editor used by many writers says it won't add AI to its default configuration, citing user privacy, and is pitching 'no AI' as a feature against Word and Docs.

items.title: Research Integrity in Scholarly Communications — SSP Pulse Check Report
items.excerpt: SSP's latest Pulse Check survey shows how scholarly publishers are dealing with research integrity as paper mills, manipulation and generative-AI-made submissions put integrity systems under strain.

items.title: Guest Post — Six Ways to Close the Attribution Loop in Publishing
items.excerpt: A six-part model for explaining spikes in manuscript submissions as discovery shifts to agentic AI and zero-click behavior, and for how publishers should reach both humans and the AI tools they use.

items.title: Can Better Wording Fix the 'Made With AI' Problem? New 2026 Research Says It's Complicated
items.excerpt: New 2026 research looks at whether rewording AI-disclosure labels changes how readers trust AI-assisted content. It matters because 'Made with AI' labels are becoming standard on books and digital media.

items.title: Another AI scandal affects an author in competition for a prestigious award
items.excerpt: Jane Friedman argues every high-profile literary award that tries to exclude AI-assisted work risks a scandal like this one (likely the same Orélien story The Bookseller covered; the article is paywalled).

items.title: Veteran Producers Launch Bookish 'Micromovie' Studio
items.excerpt: Rommi, a new studio making vertical live-action films from romance novels, launches as HarperCollins' Harlequin adapts some of its titles into AI-generated 'micro-dramas' with Bengaluru tech company Dashverse.

items.title: The Concept of the Asian Robot Maid Has Haunted My Life
items.excerpt: 'I, Roomba', an essay from Franny Choi's We Radiant Things, looks at the robot-maid trope and the rise of physical AI, drawing on industry reports on embodied AI (literary essay, a weak fit).
